indication: metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, first line
design: randomised open-label phase 3 (LMS-04), French Sarcoma Group
intervention: doxorubicin + trabectedin induction, then trabectedin maintenance
quality: low risk of bias (randomised phase 3, open-label)
intervention_dosing: doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + trabectedin 1.1 mg/m2 q3w x6, then trabectedin maintenance
inclusion_match_notes: This is the evidence behind the regimen her sarcoma oncologist has already planned, and she matches it on every axis the trial screened: metastatic leiomyosarcoma, no prior systemic therapy, uterine primaries made up a majority of the enrolled population. The trial capped performance status at ECOG 0-1, which her chart does not document; the ECOG 1 in the profile is an intake assumption. Baseline LVEF is also undocumented and is mandatory before an anthracycline.

indication: previously untreated advanced or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma
quality: low risk of bias (randomised phase 3, open-label)
intervention_dosing: gemcitabine 675 mg/m2 d1,d8 + docetaxel 75 mg/m2 d8, q3w
sponsor: University College London / Cancer Research UK
inclusion_match_notes: The first-line alternative to an anthracycline backbone, and she is eligible today on indication and line. It did not beat doxorubicin on 24-week PFS, so the value here is as a comparator for the LMS-04 decision rather than as a separate opportunity. Leiomyosarcoma made up roughly half the trial population, but the uterine subgroup was not separately powered.

indication: metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, first line
inclusion_match_notes: A direct first-line competitor to the doxorubicin/trabectedin plan, and she meets the indication and line criteria. Accrual has closed, so this is a comparison she will read about rather than a seat she can take. Lurbinectedin is approved in small-cell lung cancer, which makes an off-label conversation possible independently of the trial.

indication: unresectable or metastatic leiomyosarcoma
inclusion_match_notes: The eligibility text opens a first-line door explicitly: patients who decline standard first-line systemic therapy are eligible, so this is available during the window before LMS-04 starts as well as after it. ECOG 0-2 is wide enough that the undocumented performance status does not by itself block screening, unlike the ECOG 0-1 protocols. No biomarker gate, and archival tumor tissue is required, which the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 lung core should satisfy.

indication: advanced soft-tissue sarcoma, first line
intervention: MASCT-I (autologous dendritic cell and cytokine-induced killer cell therapy) + doxorubicin + ifosfamide
inclusion_match_notes: First-line and leiomyosarcoma is a listed histology, so the line axis matches the window she is in now. Sites are in China, which puts it outside her US geography band, and the cell product is manufactured locally. Included so the first-line cell-therapy option is on the record rather than silently absent.

indication: advanced soft-tissue sarcoma, first line
inclusion_match_notes: Checkpoint blockade added to an anthracycline backbone in the first-line setting, with leiomyosarcoma among the listed histologies. The site is in Shanghai, so access is the binding constraint rather than eligibility. Her PD-L1 status is untested, though this protocol does not gate on it.

indication: advanced bone and soft-tissue sarcoma
biomarker: B7-H3 (not required for entry)
design: phase 1b combination dose escalation and expansion (ARTEMIS-103)
intervention: HS-20093 (B7-H3 ADC) + anlotinib, epirubicin, or adebrelimab
inclusion_match_notes: One of the few B7-H3 ADC protocols with a cohort that takes patients who have had no prior treatment for advanced disease, which is the situation she is in right now. B7-H3 is on her biomarker survey and untested, though this protocol does not require it for entry. Chinese sites and a not-yet-recruiting status make the practical odds low.

indication: metastatic non-adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma after prior chemotherapy
quality: low risk of bias (randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled)
inclusion_match_notes: Approved for her disease but gated on prior chemotherapy, so it is a seat that opens after LMS-04 rather than one available now. Leiomyosarcoma was the largest histology stratum. ECOG 0-1 was required, which the undocumented performance status leaves unsettled.

indication: advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after at least two prior regimens
quality: low risk of bias (randomised phase 3, open-label)
intervention_dosing: eribulin 1.4 mg/m2 IV d1, d8 q3w
inclusion_match_notes: Requires an anthracycline plus one further regimen, so she is two lines away from this. The overall survival benefit was driven by the liposarcoma subgroup and the leiomyosarcoma subgroup did not show one, which matters for how the board weighs it in her disease. Eribulin's US label covers liposarcoma only, so leiomyosarcoma use is off-label.

indication: metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma and other sarcomas
inclusion_match_notes: A next-generation multikinase inhibitor in the same class as the approved pazopanib, with a dedicated leiomyosarcoma cohort. Prior systemic therapy is expected, so this belongs to the post-LMS-04 list. Antiangiogenic toxicity intersects with her undocumented pulmonary reserve and high-altitude baseline.

indication: advanced alveolar soft part sarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma
endpoint: objective response rate (alveolar soft part sarcoma cohort)
inclusion_match_notes: Leiomyosarcoma is one of three histology cohorts, but the registered primary endpoint sits in the alveolar soft part sarcoma arm, so the leiomyosarcoma read is secondary. Prior chemotherapy is required. Rated weak because the sarcoma cohort structure means she would be entering the part of the trial that is not driving the primary analysis.

indication: advanced leiomyosarcoma or dedifferentiated liposarcoma
biomarker: RB1 / cell-cycle pathway (correlative)
endpoint: blood thymidine kinase activity time course (phase 1) and progression-free survival (phase 2)
inclusion_match_notes: Cell-cycle blockade added to the standard second-line gemcitabine/docetaxel backbone, with leiomyosarcoma named as an eligible histology. Her RB1 status is unmeasured; a plasma assay that reported nothing is not a negative at unstated tumor fraction, and RB1 loss would bear on whether CDK4/6 inhibition makes biological sense here. Prior therapy is expected, so this sits after induction.

indication: metastatic or unresectable RB1-negative leiomyosarcoma
biomarker: RB1 loss (required)
inclusion_match_notes: Entry hinges on RB1 loss, which she has not had measured on tissue; the plasma panel reporting no RB1 alteration settles nothing at an unsupplied tumor fraction. RB1 loss is common in uterine leiomyosarcoma, so the prior is not low, and the tissue NGS the validator already ordered would answer it. Conditional on that result and on prior systemic therapy.

indication: advanced or metastatic leiomyosarcoma after standard chemotherapy
inclusion_match_notes: Requires standard-of-care chemotherapy first, with no cap on prior lines, so this opens after LMS-04. ECOG 0-2 is permissive enough that the undocumented performance status is unlikely to exclude her. PD-L1 is untested but not required.

indication: advanced leiomyosarcoma, or sarcoma with TSC1/TSC2 loss
biomarker: TSC1/TSC2 loss (alternative entry route)
inclusion_match_notes: Leiomyosarcoma patients enter on histology without needing a TSC alteration, but one prior systemic therapy is required, so this is a post-induction seat. ECOG 0-2 accommodates the undocumented performance status. Nab-sirolimus is approved in PEComa, which makes the agent obtainable off-label independent of the trial.

indication: metastatic or locally advanced leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline
inclusion_match_notes: Anthracycline exposure is mandatory, and the LMS-04 plan would give her trabectedin as part of induction, which would likely disqualify her from a trial randomising to that same agent. Italian sites. Kept so the sequencing conflict between the planned induction and later trabectedin trials is visible.

indication: advanced soft-tissue sarcoma with disease control after first-line chemotherapy
inclusion_match_notes: Addresses the same question the LMS-04 maintenance phase answers, in patients whose disease is controlled after first-line chemotherapy. She would only reach it after induction, and cumulative anthracycline exposure from LMS-04 would need accounting against the liposomal dose. Taiwanese sites put it outside her geography band.

indication: metastatic or unresectable soft-tissue sarcoma after 1-2 lines
endpoint: maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase 2 dose
inclusion_match_notes: A sarcoma-dedicated ADC that takes any histology after one to two prior cytotoxic lines, so LMS-04 alone would qualify her. ECOG 0-1 is required and hers is an assumption, which is the axis to close before screening. No biomarker gate at entry.

indication: locally advanced or metastatic sarcoma and selected solid tumors
biomarker: LRRC15 (sponsor-assessed)
inclusion_match_notes: Sarcoma patients enter with no more than two prior systemic lines, which LMS-04 alone would satisfy. A pre-treatment biopsy or archival block is mandatory and she has two specimens available. ECOG 0-1 required, so the performance-status documentation gap applies.

indication: advanced solid tumors including sarcoma
biomarker: B7-H3 (CD276), correlative
inclusion_match_notes: Sarcoma is named in the eligible tumor list and entry does not require a B7-H3 result, so she could be screened on histology alone. B7-H3 is on her biomarker survey and untested; 97% of soft-tissue sarcomas stain positive (pmid:39478506), so the prior is high but the value is unproven at entry. Archival tissue is acceptable where a fresh biopsy is unsafe.

indication: advanced or metastatic solid tumors
biomarker: B7-H3 (CD276), central testing where tissue available
intervention: GSK5764227 (risvutatug rezetecan, HS-20093), alone or with platinum or checkpoint blockade
inclusion_match_notes: A pan-tumor B7-H3 ADC programme with US sites, open to advanced solid tumors after progression on available standard therapy. Combination cohorts allow up to three prior lines, monotherapy requires exhaustion of standard options, so the line she is at determines which module fits. ECOG 0-1 with no deterioration in the preceding fortnight is required.

indication: relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma
inclusion_match_notes: Osteosarcoma only, so she cannot enrol. It is here because it is the first randomised phase 3 test of a B7-H3 ADC in a sarcoma, and the read-out is what the board will want when weighing whether a B7-H3 stain is worth ordering for her. Informational, not an option.

indication: advanced colorectal, breast, penile carcinoma and sarcoma
sponsor: German Cancer Research Center / University of Tübingen
inclusion_match_notes: Sarcoma is listed among the conditions but the registered eligibility text is written around heavily pre-treated colorectal cancer, so which sarcoma patients the sarcoma cohort actually takes is not readable from the registry. German sites. Kept because it is the only T-cell-engager format against B7-H3 that names sarcoma at all.

indication: solid tumors harbouring SWI/SNF alterations (INI1-negative cohort)
biomarker: INI1/SMARCB1 loss by IHC, or bi-allelic SMARCB1 loss by molecular testing when IHC equivocal
effect_size: 9% ORR in the INI1-negative cohort (3 partial responses of 32)
inclusion_match_notes: This is the trial route the SMARCB1 branch points at, and Cohort 3 took INI1-negative tumors of any histology, which would have covered a uterine leiomyosarcoma with confirmed INI1 loss. Two things hold it back: accrual is closed, and her SMARCB1 frameshift is a plasma call with no tissue confirmation, weighed against 170 consecutive uterine smooth-muscle tumours that all retained SMARCB1 (pmid:34271067). The 9% response rate is also a modest ceiling, and grade 3 or worse treatment-related events occurred in 10%.

indication: advanced epithelioid sarcoma with loss of INI1/SMARCB1
biomarker: INI1/SMARCB1 loss (required)
inclusion_match_notes: The basis of tazemetostat's accelerated approval, and that approval is in epithelioid sarcoma, a different histology from hers. She cannot enrol and the label does not reach her. It is in the dossier because any off-label conversation about EZH2 inhibition in an INI1-deficient leiomyosarcoma starts from this response rate and this histology gap.

indication: metastatic or recurrent solid tumors with SWI/SNF loss (Cohort 1.A: SMARCB1-defective)
biomarker: bi-allelic (homozygous) SMARCB1 deletion by validated NGS on tissue or plasma, plus centralised IHC confirmation of loss of expression
inclusion_match_notes: The live SWI/SNF basket, and its SMARCB1 cohort caps prior therapy at one line, so the sequencing works if INI1 loss is confirmed after LMS-04. Two gates are unresolved: the protocol asks for bi-allelic homozygous SMARCB1 deletion, and what she has is a single frameshift call in plasma, which is a different molecular configuration; and it requires centralised IHC showing loss of expression, which has not been done. It also requires exhaustion of standard options and sits at a French site, so US access would need sponsor discussion.

indication: relapsed or refractory SMARCB1- or SMARCA4-deficient tumors
biomarker: SMARCB1 (INI1) or SMARCA4 deficiency by institutional IHC, or molecular confirmation where IHC is equivocal
inclusion_match_notes: The eligibility list ends with 'other SMARCB1 or SMARCA4 deficient tumors', which is an explicit histology-agnostic door for a confirmed INI1-negative uterine leiomyosarcoma. Institutional IHC is the accepted evidence, so the INI1 stain the validator ordered would be the exact document required. Accrual has closed, which is why this is weak rather than partial.

indication: advanced synovial sarcoma or SMARCB1-loss tumors
biomarker: bi-allelic SMARCB1 alteration or corresponding protein loss
inclusion_match_notes: Terminated, so nothing is enrollable here. It took 'other solid tumors with SMARCB1 loss' on documented bi-allelic alteration or protein loss, which is the same door she would have knocked on. Kept so the board sees that the BRD9-degrader route into SMARCB1-deficient disease has already been tried and stopped.

indication: locally advanced or metastatic SMARCB1-perturbed solid tumors
biomarker: SMARCB1-null tumor
endpoint: frequency and severity of adverse events
inclusion_match_notes: The second BRD9 degrader to stop in SMARCB1-null disease, terminated after phase 1. Its ECOG ceiling was 2, which would have been unusually forgiving for her undocumented performance status. Included as mechanism context for how thin the SMARCB1-directed pipeline has become outside EZH2.

indication: MUC16-expressing SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma or epithelioid sarcoma
biomarker: loss of SMARCB1 by IHC plus serum CA-125 ≥ 70 U/mL or MUC16 IHC H-score > 25
intervention: ubamatamab (MUC16 x CD3 bispecific), alone or with cemiplimab
inclusion_match_notes: SMARCB1 deficiency is the platform gate, but the two cohorts are closed to renal medullary carcinoma and epithelioid sarcoma, so a uterine leiomyosarcoma is out regardless of INI1 status. Included because it shows SMARCB1-deficiency being used as an enrolment handle for an agent whose own target is unrelated, which is the pattern to watch if the INI1 stain comes back negative.

indication: recurrent or refractory PRAME-positive advanced solid tumors
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive plus PRAME expression by the sponsor's IMADetect RT-qPCR assay
intervention: IMA203 / IMA203CD8 (PRAME-directed TCR-engineered T cells), alone or with nivolumab
endpoint: maximum tolerated dose and objective response
inclusion_match_notes: Her HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed, which clears the restriction gate this whole programme is built on, and the protocol takes solid tumors without naming histologies except for the ovarian and endometrial cohorts. The second gate is PRAME expression, and the sponsor reads it by RT-qPCR on their own device rather than by IHC, so a local stain would not substitute. She also must have received or be ineligible for available standard care, which LMS-04 currently is, and ECOG 0-1 is required against an undocumented performance status.

indication: selected advanced solid tumors, PRAME-positive
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive plus PRAME-positive tumor
inclusion_match_notes: Entry is her allele plus a PRAME-positive tumor, with no cell manufacturing and no lymphodepletion, which makes it the lower-intensity way to use the same restriction. Accrual has closed, so this is now precedent rather than a seat. PRAME remains untested on her tissue.

indication: selected advanced solid tumors, MAGE-A4-expressing
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive plus MAGE-A4-positive tumor
inclusion_match_notes: An off-the-shelf antibody format riding the same HLA-A*02:01 restriction as the TCR-T products, with no apheresis and no lymphodepletion, which is a real practical difference for a patient who has not started chemotherapy. Two conditions stand between her and screening: MAGE-A4 expression, untested, and relapse from or refractoriness to standard therapy, which she has not reached. The 'selected' tumor list is not spelled out in the registry, so whether uterine leiomyosarcoma is on it needs a call to the sponsor.

indication: advanced synovial sarcoma or myxoid round-cell liposarcoma
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01/02:02/02:03/02:06 positive plus MAGE-A4 expression ≥1+ in ≥10% of cells by central IHC
effect_size: 37% overall response rate (19 of 52); 39% in synovial sarcoma
inclusion_match_notes: She clears the allele gate but not the histology one: the trial took synovial sarcoma and myxoid round-cell liposarcoma only, and the Tecelra label is narrower still at synovial sarcoma alone. Prior anthracycline or ifosfamide is also required, which she has not had. Its value here is the MAGE-A4 threshold it established, ≥1+ staining in ≥10% of cells by central IHC, which is the bar any MAGE-A4 stain she orders should be read against.

indication: NY-ESO-1-positive synovial sarcoma or myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01, A*02:05 or A*02:06 positive plus NY-ESO-1 expression by central laboratory
intervention: letetresgene autoleucel (lete-cel, NY-ESO-1 TCR-engineered T cells)
inclusion_match_notes: Enrolment is restricted to synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma, so her histology closes this regardless of her allele or any NY-ESO-1 result. Logged because it is the reference point for what NY-ESO-1-directed TCR-T achieves in sarcoma, and because it defines the central-laboratory expression assay a future stain would need to match.

indication: advanced clear cell sarcoma, HLA-A*02:01 positive
biomarker: HLA-A*02:01 positive
sponsor: Sarcoma Alliance for Research through Collaboration
inclusion_match_notes: Her allele is the entry criterion, but the histology is fixed to clear cell sarcoma, which shares melanocytic biology and therefore gp100 expression; a leiomyosarcoma does not. Not enrollable. It earns a row because it is the clearest current example of an HLA-A*02:01-gated ImmTAC being moved into a sarcoma, and it shows the pathway a leiomyosarcoma cohort would follow if an antigen were found.

indication: HLA-A*02-positive MAGE-A4-expressing carcinomas including endometrial cancer
biomarker: at least one HLA-A*02 inclusion allele plus MAGE-A4 expression by central laboratory
intervention: uzatresgene autoleucel (ADP-A2M4CD8), alone or with nivolumab or pembrolizumab
inclusion_match_notes: The histology list covers urothelial, oesophageal, gastric, lung, head and neck, ovarian, endometrial and melanoma, and a uterine sarcoma is not among them. Two of its criteria are worth carrying forward for her anyway: HLA-A*02:05 on either allele is an exclusion, and she carries A*03:01 rather than A*02:05, and it requires ≥90% room-air oxygen saturation at rest, which needs interpreting against her residence at roughly 8,500 feet before any cell-therapy screening.

indication: previously treated advanced solid tumors, tissue TMB-high
biomarker: TMB ≥10 mutations per megabase on a validated tissue assay
effect_size: 29% objective response rate in the TMB-high group (30 of 102)
inclusion_match_notes: The tumour-agnostic TMB-high approval rests on this cohort, and primary site does not enter the indication, so a TMB-high result would open it for her. TMB has not been measured: the Guardant report did not return one, and plasma TMB is unreliable at low tumour fraction anyway. The approval also requires prior therapy, so even a TMB-high result would not open this during the first-line window she is in now.

indication: TRK fusion-positive solid tumors, any histology
biomarker: NTRK1, NTRK2 or NTRK3 gene fusion
design: pooled analysis of three phase 1/2 trials
inclusion_match_notes: A fusion would make this available at any line, including the one she is at now, and sarcomas were represented in the pooled population. Her fusion status is unmeasured; plasma DNA sequencing is insensitive to fusions at low tumour fraction, so the Guardant report neither found nor excluded one. The RNA fusion panel already on the validator's tissue order settles it, and the prior probability in uterine leiomyosarcoma is low.

indication: advanced solid tumors, including a mismatch-repair-deficient basket cohort
biomarker: mismatch-repair deficiency / MSI-high
design: phase 1 dose escalation with expansion cohorts (GARNET)
endpoint: treatment-emergent adverse events and objective response
inclusion_match_notes: The mismatch-repair-deficient cohort here supports a tumour-agnostic indication that ignores primary site, so a dMMR result would matter more than the sarcoma histology. MMR and MSI are untested on her tissue and uterine leiomyosarcoma is nearly always proficient, so expect a negative; the MMR immunostains are already on the validator's single block cut, which closes the question cheaply. Accrual has closed, so any use would be off-label rather than on trial.

indication: advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after at least one prior line
biomarker: homologous recombination deficiency (correlative, not required for entry)
effect_size: 27% overall objective response rate (6 of 22); median PFS 6.9 months
intervention_dosing: olaparib 200 mg twice daily d1-7 + temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily d1-7, q21d
inclusion_match_notes: Her exact histology, and the response rate is the strongest signal any targeted combination has produced in uterine leiomyosarcoma. It requires at least one prior line, so it belongs to the post-LMS-04 list rather than the window she is in. Entry did not depend on a homologous-recombination result, but her HRD and BRCA status is unmeasured and would inform how likely she is to be in the responding subset.

indication: advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after prior therapy
inclusion_match_notes: The randomised confirmation of NCI 10250 in the same histology, which is the study that would settle whether the phase 2 response rate holds up. Prior therapy is required and accrual has closed. Worth tracking for the read-out rather than for a seat.

indication: metastatic or advanced high-grade bone and soft-tissue sarcoma
intervention: fluzoparib + camrelizumab with concurrent stereotactic body radiotherapy
inclusion_match_notes: Combines the PARP route with the radiotherapy question her oncologist has kept open for the pulmonary disease, in high-grade sarcoma of any histology after at least one systemic line. Chinese sites. The infiltrative radiologic pattern in her lungs may complicate whether her lesions are SBRT-targetable, which is a planning question independent of this protocol.

indication: relapsed and refractory advanced soft-tissue sarcoma
biomarker: FAPi PET/CT or PET/MRI uptake in a measurable lesion (required)
design: phase 1 dose escalation with imaging selection
inclusion_match_notes: A therapeutic alpha-emitter, not an imaging study: the copper-64 agent is the selection scan and the actinium-225 conjugate is the treatment. Any soft-tissue sarcoma histology qualifies after one prior regimen, and the biomarker is a FAP PET signal rather than a stain, which sidesteps the tissue-availability problem entirely. FAP is on her biomarker survey as an untested stromal target, and mesenchymal tumours carry it on the malignant cells themselves, so the prior for a positive scan is reasonable.

indication: locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors including sarcoma
biomarker: [203Pb]Pb-PSV359 SPECT/CT uptake in at least one known lesion at 1 hour
inclusion_match_notes: Sarcoma is a named condition and entry turns on a lead-203 scan showing uptake, which is a functional gate she can be tested for without another biopsy. The lead-212 arm delivers the therapeutic alpha dose, so this is a treatment protocol with an imaging selection step rather than a diagnostic study. US sites, ECOG 0-1 required, and progression on or absence of standard therapy is the line criterion.

indication: advanced solid tumors with FAP-2286 uptake
biomarker: [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET uptake (required)
inclusion_match_notes: A beta-emitting FAP radioligand open to solid tumors by uptake rather than histology, with the gallium-68 scan acting as the selection gate and the lutetium-177 conjugate as the therapy. Whether the tumour-type cohorts still open include sarcoma needs confirming with the sponsor, since the registry lists only 'solid tumor'. Crossfire from a beta emitter does not require every cell to express the target, which is the argument for keeping this class in play when expression is heterogeneous.

indication: soft-tissue sarcoma progressing after standard therapy
biomarker: [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT uptake in tumour neovasculature
inclusion_match_notes: The registered primary endpoint is an imaging measure, which reads like a diagnostic study, but a therapeutic lutetium-177 dose is administered and the target is sarcoma neovasculature rather than the tumour cell, so it is a therapy protocol under the theranostic rule. Fourteen patients, completed, Swiss single centre. Kept as proof that PSMA-directed radioligand therapy has been attempted in soft-tissue sarcoma at all, which is otherwise invisible.

indication: bilateral pulmonary metastases from bone or soft-tissue sarcoma
design: phase 1 dose escalation of in vivo lung perfusion
intervention: in vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin, plus metastasectomy
endpoint: acute lung injury after in vivo lung perfusion
inclusion_match_notes: Written for exactly her anatomy: bilateral pulmonary metastases, three or more lesions, no extrapulmonary disease, age under 65, ECOG 0-2. Two things need checking before it is real. Every lesion in the perfused lung must be resectable by wedge or segmental resection, and the infiltrative, possibly inflammatory pattern the radiologist described is the kind of finding that makes that judgement difficult; and cumulative doxorubicin above 450 mg is an exclusion, which LMS-04 induction could approach.

indication: sarcoma metastatic to the lungs
design: phase 1/2 of pulmonary suffusion with metastasectomy
intervention: pulmonary suffusion with cisplatin plus metastasectomy
inclusion_match_notes: Aimed at minimal residual disease in the lung after metastasectomy, with ECOG ≤2 and no requirement for histologic confirmation of every nodule. It presumes resectable pulmonary disease, which her infiltrative pattern puts in doubt, and it is a post-systemic-control option rather than something to do instead of induction. Kept because her oncologist explicitly left local therapy on the table for after systemic control.

indication: metastatic leiomyosarcoma and selected soft-tissue sarcomas (MFS, UPS, synovial, DDLPS)
design: phase 1 dose escalation with mandatory paired biopsies
intervention: peposertib (DNA-PK inhibitor) + low-dose pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
inclusion_match_notes: Despite the doxorubicin backbone this is not a first-line door: the protocol requires at least one prior line, so she reaches it only after LMS-04. The sharper constraint is the anthracycline cap, cumulative doxorubicin at or under 360 mg/m2 before enrolment; six full LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m2 land exactly on that limit, so whether this seat survives induction depends on cycle count and any dose reductions, and her team should know that before cycle six. ECOG up to 2 accommodates the undocumented performance status, and the mandatory biopsy needs disease amenable to sampling, which her pulmonary pattern should permit.

indication: advanced leiomyosarcoma or dedifferentiated liposarcoma
line: 1L or 2L+ (phase 2 admits systemic-treatment-naive; prior gemcitabine excluded)
biomarker: intact Rb expression by IHC on baseline or archival tumour (required)
endpoint: blood thymidine kinase activity time course (phase 1) and progression-free survival (phase 2)
inclusion_match_notes: Correction to the earlier row, which read this as post-induction only: the phase 2 portion explicitly admits systemic-treatment-naive leiomyosarcoma, so it is a live first-line alternative during the window before LMS-04 starts. Prior gemcitabine is disqualifying in phase 2, which cuts both ways - LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine and would preserve her eligibility, whereas starting gemcitabine/docetaxel instead would close this permanently. Entry requires intact Rb expression by IHC, a test she has not had; note this is the opposite gate from the RB1-loss CDK7 protocol, so one Rb stain routes her between the two. ECOG up to 2 accommodates the undocumented performance status.

indication: molecularly selected advanced solid tumors; cohort T1 was ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma
biomarker: ATRX mutation by NGS (LMS cohort); ATM, replication-stress genes, SDH in other cohorts
design: translational phase 2, four molecularly defined cohorts with paired biopsies
intervention: berzosertib (ATR inhibitor) monotherapy, 240 mg/m2 IV twice weekly
endpoint: progression-free survival and pharmacodynamic target engagement
effect_size: ATRX-mutant LMS cohort progressed within 4 months; longest disease control was in SDH-mutant GIST (median PFS 229 days)
intervention_dosing: berzosertib 240 mg/m2 IV twice per week
inclusion_match_notes: The direct clinical test of the ATR-inhibition-for-ALT idea in her exact histology: an ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma cohort built on the same ALT rationale the preclinical file carries. It read out negative for monotherapy, with progression inside 4 months despite biopsy-proven target engagement, and on-treatment SLFN11 expression rather than ATRX status tracked with what benefit there was. Her own ATRX and ALT status remain untested, so this row bounds the branch rather than closing it - the open question after this result is combinations, not more monotherapy.

indication: metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma, up to 3 prior lines
design: randomised phase 2, gemcitabine with or without berzosertib
inclusion_match_notes: The combination form of the ATR question in her histology: randomised, leiomyosarcoma-specific, chemotherapy backbone. Accrual is complete and no result is indexed yet as of August 2026, so this is a read-out to watch rather than a seat, and it is the study most likely to say whether ATR inhibition adds anything after the monotherapy cohort failed. Its ECOG ceiling was 0-1, the axis her chart leaves undocumented, and it excluded prior gemcitabine.

indication: advanced solid tumors; dose escalation admits soft-tissue sarcoma as a temozolomide standard-of-care histology
biomarker: MGMT promoter hypermethylation, or a histology where temozolomide is standard per guidelines (soft-tissue sarcoma qualifies)
design: phase 1/2, dose escalation then MSS colorectal phase 2
inclusion_match_notes: The one live US seat the ATR sweep found that she could plausibly occupy: the dose-escalation arm takes soft-tissue sarcoma without an MGMT result because temozolomide is guideline-standard in the histology. It requires progression after available therapies, so it opens after LMS-04, and the mandatory biopsy and ECOG up to 2 are both workable. Any ALT-based rationale for putting her here specifically is conditional on ATRX/ALT testing she has not had; the entry criteria themselves do not ask for it.

indication: progressive IDH-mutant grade 2-4 astrocytoma with confirmed ATRX and p53 mutation
biomarker: ATRX mutation by IHC or NGS plus p53 mutation (required)
sponsor: Grupo Español de Investigación en Neurooncología
inclusion_match_notes: Not enrollable - astrocytoma only, Spanish sites. It is the only registered trial anywhere that uses ATRX mutation as the entry gate for an ATR inhibitor, which is exactly the selection logic the preclinical ALT row proposes for her tumour type. Its read-out is the nearest future test of that thesis, and if her own tissue NGS shows ATRX loss the result becomes directly decision-relevant.
